subject: science
passage: The tuft of fine bristles that carries a dandelion seed—a structure that lets most of the air pass straight through ______ creates a stable ring of swirling air just above itself. This ring holds the seed aloft far longer than a solid parachute of the same size would, which helps explain how dandelion seeds travel for kilometers.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The words between "seed" and "creates" are extra information describing the tuft. That information opens with a dash, so it must close with a matching dash. The subject "The tuft of fine bristles" then connects to its verb "creates."
explanation.A: Incorrect. Without a closing dash, the extra information is never set off and runs straight into the verb "creates."
explanation.B: Correct. The second dash closes the pair around the extra information, so the subject "The tuft" connects to its verb "creates."
explanation.C: Incorrect. The extra information opens with a dash, so it can't close with a comma; the two marks must match.
explanation.D: Incorrect. A semicolon can't separate the subject "The tuft of fine bristles" from its verb "creates."
